description: Rubrics for the ContextOS evaluation. A trial solves an incident when every root-cause criterion is met and at least one fix is proposed.

rootCause.description: The refund history query on payment_transactions filtered by payment_id is slow because payment_id has no index (it scans the table).
A surge of refunds from the refund batch ran that slow query, holding database connections until payment-service's connection pool was exhausted, so charges failed.
The payment-service v2.16.0 deploy, made minutes before the incident, introduced the failure.
The failure is a NullPointerException in PaymentService.charge (the payment or receipt handling changed by the deploy), not a database, dependency or capacity problem.

fix.description: Roll back or revert the v2.16.0 deploy (or ship a fix for the null handling in PaymentService.charge).

rootCause.description: The third-party fraud-api became very slow (latency of many seconds).
payment-service charges fail because the fraud check call (HttpFraudCheckClient, POST /check to fraud-api) times out, not because of payment-service's own code, its database or a deploy.

fix.description: Protect the fraud-api call with a shorter timeout, a circuit breaker or a fallback (for example fail open or queue for review), and/or escalate to the fraud-api provider.

rootCause.description: The configuration change that reduced payment-service's database connection pool (maximum-pool-size from 50 to 5) exhausted the pool, so charges could not get a connection.
The database itself is healthy: queries are not slow, so this is not a slow query, missing index or database overload.

fix.description: Revert the configuration change / restore maximum-pool-size to 50 (or another adequate size).
